title: Lazy-create auxiliary Tauri windows
description: Lazy-create nonessential JasonShell auxiliary Tauri windows instead of creating all hidden panels during startup. Problem: FN-004 found `shell_windows::create_shell_windows` eagerly creates 13 WebView2 windows, most hidden, which likely dominates cold startup memory and startup time. Target metric: reduce startup WebView2 count/native memory and time to visible top/bottom AppBars. Likely file scope: `src-tauri/src/shell_windows.rs`, panel show/hide modules (`search_panel`, `stack_popup`, `process_manager`, `terminal_panel`, etc.), capability/window tests. Acceptance criteria: top and bottom bars still start and reserve AppBars; each auxiliary panel is created on first open and works on subsequent open/hide/focus-loss cycles; startup/window-count timing is documented before/after; full validation passes; Windows smoke checklist covers all panels.

steps.name: Add a central lazy shell-window creation contract
Migrate panel and preview callers to lazy ensure before first use
Verify contracts, capabilities, and startup behavior
Windows smoke coverage for all lazy panels

log.outcome: The specification is clear, concrete, and well-scoped for the intended lifecycle change. It correctly identifies the current eager creation path in `src-tauri/src/shell_windows.rs`, the auxiliary panel modules that currently assume existing windows, and the label/contract preservation requirements. The steps are verifiable and include real automated Rust tests plus full validation gates.

The specification is clear, concrete, and well aligned with the current code: `src-tauri/src/shell_windows.rs` eagerly creates top/bottom plus all auxiliary windows today, and many panel modules currently assume auxiliary windows already exist via `get_webview_window(...).ok_or_else(...)`. The steps are verifiable, require real automated source-contract/Rust tests, preserve labels/events/capabilities, and include manual Windows smoke plus startup metrics documentation.
